addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

49		// MaxItems is the maximum number of items allowed in the cache.
50		MaxItems int

52		// OnEviction is called when an item is evicted from the cache.
53		OnEviction func(key string, value any)

56	// DefaultConfig returns a default configuration for the cache.
57	func DefaultConfig() Config {
58		return Config{
59			DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
60			CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
61			MaxItems:        1000,
62			OnEviction:      nil,
63		}
64	}
65	
66	// Cache is a thread-safe in-memory cache with TTL and memory management.
67	type Cache struct {
68		itemCount  atomic.Int64 // Use atomic operations to track item count
69		data       sync.Map
70		config     Config
71		stopChan   chan struct{}
72		closedChan chan struct{}
73	}
74	
75	// New creates a new memory cache with the given configuration.
76	func New(config Config) *Cache {
77		c := &Cache{
78			config:     config,
79			stopChan:   make(chan struct{}),
80			closedChan: make(chan struct{}),
81		}

84		return c

87	// NewDefault creates a new memory cache with default configuration.
88	func NewDefault() *Cache {

92	// Set adds a value to the cache with the default TTL.
93	func (c *Cache) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, value any) {

95	}

97	// SetWithTTL adds a value to the cache with a custom TTL.
98	func (c *Cache) SetWithTTL(_ context.Context, key string, value any, ttl time.Duration) {

100		size := estimateSize(value)
101

103		if _, exists := c.data.Load(key); exists {
104			c.data.Delete(key)
105		} else {
106			// Only increment if this is a new key.
107			(&c.itemCount).Add(1)
108		}
109	
110		c.data.Store(key, item{
111			value:      value,
112			expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl),
113			size:       size,
114		})

123	func (c *Cache) Get(_ context.Context, key string) (any, bool) {

127		}

187	func (c *Cache) Close() error {
188		select {

191			return nil
192		default:
193			close(c.stopChan)
194			<-c.closedChan // Wait for cleanup goroutine to exit
195			return nil

197	}

199	// cleanupLoop periodically cleans up expired items.
200	func (c *Cache) cleanupLoop() {
201		ticker := time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)
202		defer func() {
203			ticker.Stop()
204			close(c.closedChan)
205		}()
206	
207		for {
208			select {
209			case <-ticker.C:
210				c.cleanup()
211			case <-c.stopChan:
212				return
213			}
214		}
215	}
216	
217	// cleanup removes expired items.
218	func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
219		evicted := make(map[string]any)
220		count := 0
221	
222		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
223			itm, ok := value.(item)
224			if !ok {
225				return true
226			}
227			if time.Now().After(itm.expiration) {
228				c.data.Delete(key)
229				count++
230	
231				if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
232					if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok {
233						evicted[keyStr] = itm.value
234					}
235				}
236			}
237			return true
238		})
239	
240		if count > 0 {
241			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(count))
242	
243			// Call eviction callbacks outside the loop to avoid blocking the range
244			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
245				for k, v := range evicted {
246					c.config.OnEviction(k, v)
247				}
248			}
249		}
250	}

252	// cleanupOldest removes the oldest items if we're over the max items.
253	func (c *Cache) cleanupOldest() {
254		// Remove 20% of max items at once
255		threshold := max(c.config.MaxItems/5, 1)
256	
257		currentCount := (&c.itemCount).Load()
258	
259		// If we're not over the threshold, don't do anything
260		if currentCount <= int64(c.config.MaxItems) {
261			return
262		}
263	
264		// Find the oldest items
265		type keyExpPair struct {
266			key        string
267			value      any
268			expiration time.Time
269		}
270		candidates := make([]keyExpPair, 0, threshold)
271	
272		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
273			itm, ok := value.(item)
274			if !ok {
275				return true
276			}
277			if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok && len(candidates) < threshold {
278				candidates = append(candidates, keyExpPair{keyStr, itm.value, itm.expiration})
279				return true
280			}
281	
282			// Find the newest item in candidates
283			newestIdx := 0
284			for i := 1; i < len(candidates); i++ {
285				if candidates[i].expiration.After(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
286					newestIdx = i
287				}
288			}
289	
290			// Replace it if this item is older
291			if itm.expiration.Before(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
292				candidates[newestIdx] = keyExpPair{key.(string), itm.value, itm.expiration}
293			}
294	
295			return true
296		})
297	
298		// Delete the oldest items
299		deletedCount := 0
300		for _, candidate := range candidates {
301			c.data.Delete(candidate.key)
302			deletedCount++
303	
304			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
305				c.config.OnEviction(candidate.key, candidate.value)
306			}
307		}
308	
309		// Update count
310		if deletedCount > 0 {
311			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(deletedCount))
312		}
313	}

315	// estimateSize attempts to estimate the memory footprint of a value.
316	func estimateSize(value any) int {
317		switch v := value.(type) {
318		case string:
319			return len(v) + 24 // base size + string overhead
320		case []byte:
321			return len(v) + 24 // base size + slice overhead
322		case map[string]any:
323			return len(v) * 64 // rough estimate
324		default:
325			return 64 // default conservative estimate
326		}
327	}

12	// Schedule represents a parsed cron expression.
13	type Schedule struct {
14		seconds  fieldMatcher // 0-59 (optional, for 6-field format)
15		minutes  fieldMatcher // 0-59
16		hours    fieldMatcher // 0-23
17		days     fieldMatcher // 1-31

28	// ParseCronExpression parses a cron expression and returns a Schedule.
29	// Supports both 5-field (minute hour day month weekday) and 6-field (second minute hour day month weekday) formats.
30	func ParseCronExpression(expr string) (*Schedule, error) {
31		if expr == "" {
32			return nil, errors.New("empty cron expression")
33		}
34	
35		fields := strings.Fields(expr)
36		if len(fields) != 5 && len(fields) != 6 {
37			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid cron expression: expected 5 or 6 fields, got %d", len(fields))
38		}

40		s := &Schedule{
41			hasSecs: len(fields) == 6,
42		}
43	
44		var err error
45		offset := 0
46	
47		// Parse seconds (if 6-field format)
48		if s.hasSecs {
49			s.seconds, err = parseField(fields[0], 0, 59)
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid seconds field")
52			}
53			offset = 1
54		} else {
55			s.seconds = &exactMatcher{value: 0} // Default to 0 seconds
56		}
57	
58		// Parse minutes
59		s.minutes, err = parseField(fields[offset], 0, 59)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid minutes field")
62		}
63	
64		// Parse hours
65		s.hours, err = parseField(fields[offset+1], 0, 23)
66		if err != nil {
67			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid hours field")
68		}
69	
70		// Parse days
71		s.days, err = parseField(fields[offset+2], 1, 31)
72		if err != nil {
73			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid days field")
74		}
75	
76		// Parse months
77		s.months, err = parseField(fields[offset+3], 1, 12)
78		if err != nil {
79			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid months field")
80		}

98		}

101		maxTime := from.AddDate(4, 0, 0)
102	
103		for from.Before(maxTime) {

106			}
107	
108			// Advance to next potential match
109			if s.hasSecs {

111			} else {
112				from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute)
113			}

120	// matches checks if the given time matches the schedule.
121	func (s *Schedule) matches(t time.Time) bool {
122		return s.seconds.matches(t.Second()) &&
123			s.minutes.matches(t.Minute()) &&
124			s.hours.matches(t.Hour()) &&
125			s.months.matches(int(t.Month())) &&
126			(s.days.matches(t.Day()) || s.weekdays.matches(int(t.Weekday())))
127	}

129	// parseField parses a single cron field (supports *, ranges, lists, steps).
130	func parseField(field string, min, max int) (fieldMatcher, error) {
131		// Wildcard
132		if field == "*" {
133			return &wildcardMatcher{}, nil
134		}
135	
136		// Step values (*/N)
137		if strings.HasPrefix(field, "*/") {
138			step, err := strconv.Atoi(field[2:])
139			if err != nil || step < 1 || step > max {
140				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid step value: %s", field)
141			}
142			return &stepMatcher{step: step, min: min, max: max}, nil
143		}
144	
145		// List (1,2,3)
146		if strings.Contains(field, ",") {
147			parts := strings.Split(field, ",")
148			values := make([]int, 0, len(parts))
149			for _, p := range parts {
150				val, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(p))
151				if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
152					return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid list value: %s", p)
153				}
154				values = append(values, val)
155			}
156			return &listMatcher{values: values}, nil
157		}
158	
159		// Range (1-5)
160		if strings.Contains(field, "-") {
161			parts := strings.Split(field, "-")
162			if len(parts) != 2 {
163				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
164			}
165			start, err1 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
166			end, err2 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
167			if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || start < min || end > max || start > end {
168				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
169			}
170			return &rangeMatcher{start: start, end: end}, nil
171		}
172	
173		// Exact value
174		val, err := strconv.Atoi(field)
175		if err != nil || val < min || val > max {

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)

110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {

113		}

115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}

122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {

154		// Create a separate context for each background runner

53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3

12	// Schedule represents a parsed cron expression.
13	type Schedule struct {
14		seconds  fieldMatcher // 0-59 (optional, for 6-field format)
15		minutes  fieldMatcher // 0-59
16		hours    fieldMatcher // 0-23
17		days     fieldMatcher // 1-31

21	}

28	// ParseCronExpression parses a cron expression and returns a Schedule.
29	// Supports both 5-field (minute hour day month weekday) and 6-field (second minute hour day month weekday) formats.
30	func ParseCronExpression(expr string) (*Schedule, error) {
31		if expr == "" {
32			return nil, errors.New("empty cron expression")
33		}
34	
35		fields := strings.Fields(expr)
36		if len(fields) != 5 && len(fields) != 6 {
37			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid cron expression: expected 5 or 6 fields, got %d", len(fields))
38		}
39	
40		s := &Schedule{
41			hasSecs: len(fields) == 6,
42		}
43	
44		var err error
45		offset := 0
46	
47		// Parse seconds (if 6-field format)
48		if s.hasSecs {
49			s.seconds, err = parseField(fields[0], 0, 59)
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid seconds field")
52			}
53			offset = 1
54		} else {
55			s.seconds = &exactMatcher{value: 0} // Default to 0 seconds
56		}
57	
58		// Parse minutes
59		s.minutes, err = parseField(fields[offset], 0, 59)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid minutes field")
62		}
63	
64		// Parse hours
65		s.hours, err = parseField(fields[offset+1], 0, 23)
66		if err != nil {
67			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid hours field")
68		}
69	
70		// Parse days
71		s.days, err = parseField(fields[offset+2], 1, 31)
72		if err != nil {
73			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid days field")
74		}
75	
76		// Parse months
77		s.months, err = parseField(fields[offset+3], 1, 12)
78		if err != nil {
79			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid months field")
80		}

91	// Next returns the next time the schedule should run after the given time.
92	func (s *Schedule) Next(from time.Time) time.Time {
93		// Start from the next second/minute
94		if s.hasSecs {
95			from = from.Add(1 * time.Second).Truncate(time.Second)
96		} else {
97			from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute).Truncate(time.Minute)
98		}
99	
100		// Cap search at 4 years to prevent infinite loops
101		maxTime := from.AddDate(4, 0, 0)
102	
103		for from.Before(maxTime) {
104			if s.matches(from) {
105				return from
106			}
107	
108			// Advance to next potential match
109			if s.hasSecs {
110				from = from.Add(1 * time.Second)
111			} else {
112				from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute)
113			}
114		}

121	func (s *Schedule) matches(t time.Time) bool {
122		return s.seconds.matches(t.Second()) &&
123			s.minutes.matches(t.Minute()) &&
124			s.hours.matches(t.Hour()) &&
125			s.months.matches(int(t.Month())) &&
126			(s.days.matches(t.Day()) || s.weekdays.matches(int(t.Weekday())))
127	}

129	// parseField parses a single cron field (supports *, ranges, lists, steps).
130	func parseField(field string, min, max int) (fieldMatcher, error) {
131		// Wildcard
132		if field == "*" {
133			return &wildcardMatcher{}, nil
134		}
135	
136		// Step values (*/N)
137		if strings.HasPrefix(field, "*/") {
138			step, err := strconv.Atoi(field[2:])
139			if err != nil || step < 1 || step > max {
140				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid step value: %s", field)
141			}
142			return &stepMatcher{step: step, min: min, max: max}, nil
143		}
144	
145		// List (1,2,3)
146		if strings.Contains(field, ",") {
147			parts := strings.Split(field, ",")
148			values := make([]int, 0, len(parts))
149			for _, p := range parts {
150				val, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(p))
151				if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
152					return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid list value: %s", p)
153				}
154				values = append(values, val)
155			}
156			return &listMatcher{values: values}, nil
157		}
158	
159		// Range (1-5)
160		if strings.Contains(field, "-") {
161			parts := strings.Split(field, "-")
162			if len(parts) != 2 {
163				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
164			}
165			start, err1 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
166			end, err2 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
167			if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || start < min || end > max || start > end {
168				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
169			}
170			return &rangeMatcher{start: start, end: end}, nil
171		}
172	
173		// Exact value
174		val, err := strconv.Atoi(field)
175		if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
176			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid value: %s (must be between %d and %d)", field, min, max)
177		}
178		return &exactMatcher{value: val}, nil
179	}

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{

52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))

55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {

58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey

64		s.Secret = secret

66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")

88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}

153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)

166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)

169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)

171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}

176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {

184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})

188			close(done)

191		select {

193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}

53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3

6		"time"
7	
8		"github.com/pkg/errors"
9	)
10	
11	// Scheduler manages scheduled jobs.
12	type Scheduler struct {
13		jobs       map[string]*registeredJob
14		jobsMu     sync.RWMutex
15		timezone   *time.Location
16		middleware Middleware
17		running    bool
18		runningMu  sync.RWMutex
19		stopCh     chan struct{}
20		wg         sync.WaitGroup
21	}
22	
23	// registeredJob wraps a Job with runtime state.
24	type registeredJob struct {
25		job      *Job
26		cancelFn context.CancelFunc
27	}
28	
29	// Option configures a Scheduler.
30	type Option func(*Scheduler)
31	
32	// WithTimezone sets the default timezone for all jobs.
33	func WithTimezone(tz string) Option {
34		return func(s *Scheduler) {
35			loc, err := time.LoadLocation(tz)
36			if err != nil {
37				// Default to UTC on invalid timezone
38				loc = time.UTC
39			}
40			s.timezone = loc
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// WithMiddleware sets middleware to wrap all job handlers.
45	func WithMiddleware(mw ...Middleware) Option {
46		return func(s *Scheduler) {
47			if len(mw) > 0 {
48				s.middleware = Chain(mw...)
49			}
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// New creates a new Scheduler with optional configuration.
54	func New(opts ...Option) *Scheduler {
55		s := &Scheduler{
56			jobs:     make(map[string]*registeredJob),
57			timezone: time.UTC,
58			stopCh:   make(chan struct{}),
59		}
60	
61		for _, opt := range opts {
62			opt(s)
63		}
64	
65		return s
66	}
67	
68	// Register adds a job to the scheduler.
69	// Jobs must be registered before calling Start().
70	func (s *Scheduler) Register(job *Job) error {
71		if job == nil {
72			return errors.New("job cannot be nil")
73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")
77		}
78	
79		s.jobsMu.Lock()
80		defer s.jobsMu.Unlock()
81	
82		if _, exists := s.jobs[job.Name]; exists {
83			return errors.Errorf("job with name %q already registered", job.Name)
84		}
85	
86		s.jobs[job.Name] = &registeredJob{job: job}
87		return nil
88	}
89	
90	// Start begins executing scheduled jobs.
91	func (s *Scheduler) Start() error {
92		s.runningMu.Lock()
93		defer s.runningMu.Unlock()
94	
95		if s.running {
96			return errors.New("scheduler already running")
97		}
98	
99		s.jobsMu.RLock()
100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
101	
102		// Parse and schedule all jobs
103		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
104			schedule, err := ParseCronExpression(rj.job.Schedule)
105			if err != nil {
106				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to parse schedule for job %q", rj.job.Name)
107			}
108	
109			ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
110			rj.cancelFn = cancel
111	
112			s.wg.Add(1)
113			go s.runJobWithSchedule(ctx, rj, schedule)
114		}
115	
116		s.running = true
117		return nil
118	}
119	
120	// runJobWithSchedule executes a job according to its cron schedule.
121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {
122		defer s.wg.Done()
123	
124		// Apply middleware to handler
125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time
132			now := time.Now()
133			if rj.job.Timezone != "" {
134				loc, err := time.LoadLocation(rj.job.Timezone)
135				if err == nil {
136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146

67	type Cache struct {

75	// New creates a new memory cache with the given configuration.
76	func New(config Config) *Cache {

92	// Set adds a value to the cache with the default TTL.

97	// SetWithTTL adds a value to the cache with a custom TTL.
98	func (c *Cache) SetWithTTL(_ context.Context, key string, value any, ttl time.Duration) {
99		// Estimate size of the item (very rough approximation).
100		size := estimateSize(value)

103		if _, exists := c.data.Load(key); exists {
104			c.data.Delete(key)
105		} else {
106			// Only increment if this is a new key.
107			(&c.itemCount).Add(1)
108		}

110		c.data.Store(key, item{
111			value:      value,
112			expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl),
113			size:       size,

122	// Get retrieves a value from the cache.
123	func (c *Cache) Get(_ context.Context, key string) (any, bool) {
124		value, ok := c.data.Load(key)

149	// Delete removes a value from the cache.
150	func (c *Cache) Delete(_ context.Context, key string) {
151		if value, loaded := c.data.LoadAndDelete(key); loaded {
152			(&c.itemCount).Add(-1)

154			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {

162	// Clear removes all values from the cache.
163	func (c *Cache) Clear(_ context.Context) {
164		count := 0
165		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
166			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {

171					}
172				}
173			}
174			c.data.Delete(key)
175			count++

177		})

187	func (c *Cache) Close() error {
188		select {
189		case <-c.stopChan:

191			return nil
192		default:
193			close(c.stopChan)

199	// cleanupLoop periodically cleans up expired items.
200	func (c *Cache) cleanupLoop() {
201		ticker := time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)
202		defer func() {
203			ticker.Stop()
204			close(c.closedChan)
205		}()
206	
207		for {
208			select {
209			case <-ticker.C:
210				c.cleanup()
211			case <-c.stopChan:
212				return
213			}
214		}
215	}

217	// cleanup removes expired items.
218	func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
219		evicted := make(map[string]any)
220		count := 0
221	
222		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
223			itm, ok := value.(item)
224			if !ok {
225				return true
226			}
227			if time.Now().After(itm.expiration) {
228				c.data.Delete(key)
229				count++
230	
231				if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
232					if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok {
233						evicted[keyStr] = itm.value
234					}
235				}
236			}
237			return true
238		})
239	
240		if count > 0 {
241			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(count))
242	
243			// Call eviction callbacks outside the loop to avoid blocking the range
244			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
245				for k, v := range evicted {
246					c.config.OnEviction(k, v)
247				}
248			}
249		}
250	}

252	// cleanupOldest removes the oldest items if we're over the max items.
253	func (c *Cache) cleanupOldest() {
254		// Remove 20% of max items at once
255		threshold := max(c.config.MaxItems/5, 1)
256	
257		currentCount := (&c.itemCount).Load()
258	
259		// If we're not over the threshold, don't do anything
260		if currentCount <= int64(c.config.MaxItems) {
261			return
262		}
263	
264		// Find the oldest items
265		type keyExpPair struct {
266			key        string
267			value      any
268			expiration time.Time
269		}
270		candidates := make([]keyExpPair, 0, threshold)
271	
272		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
273			itm, ok := value.(item)

276			}

278				candidates = append(candidates, keyExpPair{keyStr, itm.value, itm.expiration})

280			}

282			// Find the newest item in candidates
283			newestIdx := 0
284			for i := 1; i < len(candidates); i++ {
285				if candidates[i].expiration.After(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
286					newestIdx = i
287				}

290			// Replace it if this item is older

295			return true

299		deletedCount := 0
300		for _, candidate := range candidates {
301			c.data.Delete(candidate.key)

304			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
305				c.config.OnEviction(candidate.key, candidate.value)
306			}
307		}
308	
309		// Update count
310		if deletedCount > 0 {
311			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(deletedCount))
312		}
313	}

12	// Schedule represents a parsed cron expression.
13	type Schedule struct {
14		seconds  fieldMatcher // 0-59 (optional, for 6-field format)
15		minutes  fieldMatcher // 0-59
16		hours    fieldMatcher // 0-23
17		days     fieldMatcher // 1-31
18		months   fieldMatcher // 1-12
19		weekdays fieldMatcher // 0-7 (0 and 7 are Sunday)
20		hasSecs  bool
21	}
22	
23	// fieldMatcher determines if a field value matches.
24	type fieldMatcher interface {
25		matches(value int) bool
26	}
27	
28	// ParseCronExpression parses a cron expression and returns a Schedule.
29	// Supports both 5-field (minute hour day month weekday) and 6-field (second minute hour day month weekday) formats.
30	func ParseCronExpression(expr string) (*Schedule, error) {
31		if expr == "" {
32			return nil, errors.New("empty cron expression")
33		}
34	
35		fields := strings.Fields(expr)
36		if len(fields) != 5 && len(fields) != 6 {
37			return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid cron expression: expected 5 or 6 fields, got %d", len(fields))
38		}
39	
40		s := &Schedule{
41			hasSecs: len(fields) == 6,
42		}
43	
44		var err error
45		offset := 0
46	
47		// Parse seconds (if 6-field format)
48		if s.hasSecs {
49			s.seconds, err = parseField(fields[0], 0, 59)
50			if err != nil {
51				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid seconds field")
52			}
53			offset = 1
54		} else {
55			s.seconds = &exactMatcher{value: 0} // Default to 0 seconds
56		}
57	
58		// Parse minutes
59		s.minutes, err = parseField(fields[offset], 0, 59)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid minutes field")
62		}
63	
64		// Parse hours
65		s.hours, err = parseField(fields[offset+1], 0, 23)
66		if err != nil {
67			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid hours field")
68		}
69	
70		// Parse days
71		s.days, err = parseField(fields[offset+2], 1, 31)
72		if err != nil {
73			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid days field")
74		}
75	
76		// Parse months
77		s.months, err = parseField(fields[offset+3], 1, 12)
78		if err != nil {
79			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid months field")
80		}
81	
82		// Parse weekdays (0-7, where both 0 and 7 represent Sunday)
83		s.weekdays, err = parseField(fields[offset+4], 0, 7)
84		if err != nil {
85			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid weekdays field")
86		}
87	
88		return s, nil
89	}

91	// Next returns the next time the schedule should run after the given time.
92	func (s *Schedule) Next(from time.Time) time.Time {
93		// Start from the next second/minute
94		if s.hasSecs {
95			from = from.Add(1 * time.Second).Truncate(time.Second)
96		} else {
97			from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute).Truncate(time.Minute)
98		}
99	
100		// Cap search at 4 years to prevent infinite loops
101		maxTime := from.AddDate(4, 0, 0)
102	
103		for from.Before(maxTime) {
104			if s.matches(from) {
105				return from
106			}
107	
108			// Advance to next potential match
109			if s.hasSecs {
110				from = from.Add(1 * time.Second)
111			} else {
112				from = from.Add(1 * time.Minute)
113			}
114		}
115	
116		// Should never reach here with valid cron expressions
117		return time.Time{}
118	}

120	// matches checks if the given time matches the schedule.
121	func (s *Schedule) matches(t time.Time) bool {
122		return s.seconds.matches(t.Second()) &&
123			s.minutes.matches(t.Minute()) &&
124			s.hours.matches(t.Hour()) &&
125			s.months.matches(int(t.Month())) &&
126			(s.days.matches(t.Day()) || s.weekdays.matches(int(t.Weekday())))
127	}

129	// parseField parses a single cron field (supports *, ranges, lists, steps).
130	func parseField(field string, min, max int) (fieldMatcher, error) {
131		// Wildcard
132		if field == "*" {
133			return &wildcardMatcher{}, nil
134		}
135	
136		// Step values (*/N)
137		if strings.HasPrefix(field, "*/") {
138			step, err := strconv.Atoi(field[2:])
139			if err != nil || step < 1 || step > max {
140				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid step value: %s", field)
141			}
142			return &stepMatcher{step: step, min: min, max: max}, nil
143		}
144	
145		// List (1,2,3)
146		if strings.Contains(field, ",") {
147			parts := strings.Split(field, ",")
148			values := make([]int, 0, len(parts))
149			for _, p := range parts {
150				val, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(p))
151				if err != nil || val < min || val > max {
152					return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid list value: %s", p)
153				}
154				values = append(values, val)
155			}
156			return &listMatcher{values: values}, nil
157		}
158	
159		// Range (1-5)
160		if strings.Contains(field, "-") {
161			parts := strings.Split(field, "-")
162			if len(parts) != 2 {
163				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
164			}
165			start, err1 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
166			end, err2 := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
167			if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || start < min || end > max || start > end {
168				return nil, errors.Errorf("invalid range: %s", field)
169			}
170			return &rangeMatcher{start: start, end: end}, nil
171		}
